summary: This note is the Snowflake documentation page for the UNDROP ICEBERG TABLE command, which restores a dropped Iceberg table. It gives the syntax, the single <name> parameter, usage notes on schema scope, name conflicts, external volumes and catalog integrations, and one example restoring my_iceberg_table. The command is available to all accounts.
one_line: Snowflake reference for the UNDROP ICEBERG TABLE command, which restores a dropped Iceberg table and its usage constraints.
key_facts: UNDROP ICEBERG TABLE is available to all accounts.
The syntax is UNDROP ICEBERG TABLE <name>.
The <name> parameter specifies the identifier for the table to restore.
Identifiers containing spaces or special characters must be enclosed in double quotes.
Identifiers enclosed in double quotes are case-sensitive.
Restoring Iceberg tables is only supported in the current schema or current database, even if the table name is fully-qualified.
If an Iceberg table with the same name already exists, an error is returned.
To undrop an Iceberg table whose external volume has been dropped, the external volume must be undropped first.
An Iceberg table cannot be undropped by creating a new external volume with the same name as the dropped external volume.
A table that uses a catalog integration cannot be restored if the associated catalog integration has been dropped.
The example UNDROP ICEBERG TABLE my_iceberg_table; restores the most recent version of a dropped table named my_iceberg_table.
The page refers to Iceberg tables as simply 'tables' except where specifying Iceberg tables avoids confusion.
